checks: A drifted browser grant stops the entire draft. The reviewed predecessor accepts it.
A separately connected reply in another Circle waited on the real pair lock and failed after the block committed.
The two members cannot retrieve one another’s safety text. The author and assigned reviewer keep their separate access.
The shared block hides both directions, preserves independent replies and appears in the owner’s block list.
Browser roles cannot execute the block routine and the app service role has no raw block-table access.
A full restore preserves the block and reply tree. The new reference refuses a restore missing the private revision function.
An owner unblock restores current visibility and the old block request cannot reapply it.
browserStories: The compiled phone-width web archive clears the draft and every old card on confirmation. Reload preserves the third member’s reply.
The compiled browser clears old content after a lost reply and leaves the result unconfirmed even though SQL saved the block.
The compiled Quest Browser connects the signed fixture wallet, checks the selected author, and reloads the same blocked thread.
The compiled Quest room renders the independent reply in simulated WebXR after the same member block.
scope: Compiled web and Quest Browser used signed test accounts and disposable SQL. The immersive room used a simulated WebXR session. Phone controllers used the canonical HTTP handlers and isolated SQL. Physical device, hosted rollout and retention review remain open.
